R can be used as a shell by pointing to the `R` binary. Use `--quiet` to suppress the startup message:

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    shell: R
    shell-args: ["--no-save", "--no-restore", "--quiet"]
    prompt: "`>`"
    ps2: "`+`"
```

Note: wrap `>` and `+` in backticks since pandoc interprets bare `>` as a blockquote marker and `+` as a list item.

## Basic Usage

```{term}
cat("Hello from R", R.version.string, "\n")
```

## Vectors and Arithmetic

```{term}
x <- 1:10
mean(x)
sd(x)
```

## Data Frames

```{term}
df <- data.frame(name = c("Alice", "Bob", "Carol"), age = c(30, 25, 35))
df[df$age > 26, ]
```

## Functions

```{term}
fibonacci <- function(n) {
  a <- 0; b <- 1
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    tmp <- b
    b <- a + b
    a <- tmp
  }
  a
}
sapply(1:10, fibonacci)
```

## Apply and Pipes

```{term}
mtcars |> head(5) |> subset(select = c(mpg, cyl, hp))
```
